The staged patch and the saved crash stack still map cleanly to this checkout at `lib/curl_fnmatch.c:135`, `lib/ftplistparser.c:297`, and `lib/ftp.c:3755`, so all source anchors below are resolved against the staged checkout.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42505099 (curl): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_ftp [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42505099
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt_results/arvo_42505099/_work/src/curl` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact `poc` with SHA-256 `4b784ee01e409b2f6db5bc8ea3bec06299636ae53c89069d7a7304e10bfec02c`. Its first TLV is type `1` (`URL`) with 37 value bytes `ftp://127.0.0.1:8991/test-list/*[][\0*`, so the effective C-string URL consumed by libcurl ends at the embedded NUL with path suffix `/test-list/*[][`. The final TLV is type `33` (`WILDCARDMATCH`) with 4-byte value `1`, and the intervening FTP reply TLVs drive the client through login/CWD/EPSV/TYPE/LIST until `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` filters a parsed directory entry. `init_wc_data()` duplicates the wildcard suffix into `wildcard->pattern`, the same heap allocation named by AddressSanitizer. `Curl_fnmatch()` sees the leading `*` and recurses into the subpattern `[][`. `setcharset()` accepts the first `]` and the next `[` as literal charset members, reaches `CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBRLEFTBR` with its cursor on the terminating NUL, then fails to reject `!c` before the state switch. In that state the terminator falls into the generic else-arm, `charset[0] = 1` executes, `(*p)++` moves past the heap string, and the next iteration dereferences one byte past the end at `lib/curl_fnmatch.c:135`. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` with stack `setcharset -> loop -> loop -> ftp_pl_insert_finfo`; the fix inserts `if(!c) return SETCHARSET_FAIL;` before the state machine.

source.description: Source. `init_wc_data()` splits the attacker-controlled FTP URL path at the last slash and duplicates the trailing wildcard component into `wildcard->pattern`, the heap string later parsed by `Curl_fnmatch()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a curl_fuzzer TLV stream. Its type-1 URL TLV has value bytes `ftp://127.0.0.1:8991/test-list/*[][\0*`, so the effective C-string URL libcurl consumes ends with `/test-list/*[][`. The same `poc` ends with a type-33 `WILDCARDMATCH` TLV whose 4-byte value is `1`, enabling FTP wildcard matching on that path.
source.note: This is the first project statement that materializes the vulnerability-relevant pattern buffer. The libFuzzer entry and the fuzzer TLV parser only stage the URL and option bytes and are the unscored harness boundary.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: In `CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBRLEFTBR`, any non-']' byte falls into the generic else-arm. When the pattern has already ended and `c == '\0'`, the missing all-state `!c` guard lets this branch treat the terminator as data and advance `*p` past the allocated string.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds `if(!c) return SETCHARSET_FAIL;` immediately after `c = **p;`, preventing this `c == '\0'` path in every state and making the later per-state NUL checks redundant.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After step 7 advances `*p` past the string terminator, the next `setcharset()` loop iteration dereferences one byte beyond the heap buffer.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the heap region allocated from `init_wc_data()`.

parser_admitted.description: The wildcard path is admitted only when the final URL path component is non-empty. For the witness the component after the last slash is `*[][`, so this guard is false and curl allocates `wildcard->pattern` instead of treating the URL as a plain directory listing.
parser_admitted.note: The harness-side TLVs also set `CURLOPT_WILDCARDMATCH = 1` and script an FTP `LIST` exchange, which is why `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` later reaches `Curl_fnmatch()` on the staged run.

tainted_value_origin.description: This `strdup()` materializes the exact heap string later over-read by `setcharset()`. On the witnessed path the duplicated final path component ends with `*[][`, so the bytes after the opening `[` are `']'`, `'['`, and the terminating NUL.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged TLV witness, the effective C-string URL is `ftp://127.0.0.1:8991/test-list/*[][`. Splitting that URL path at the final slash makes `last_slash` point to the wildcard suffix duplicated here into `wildcard->pattern`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved ASan allocation context points to this exact `strdup()` site, confirming that the later over-read comes from the same heap pattern buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The non-empty final URL path component is duplicated into `wildcard->pattern`. For the exact witness, the effective C-string URL ends in `/test-list/*[][`, so `last_slash` designates the wildcard suffix and the later ASan allocation context originates at this `strdup()`.

`ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` resolves the default callback to `Curl_fnmatch()` and passes it the heap pattern from step 1 while filtering a parsed FTP `LIST` entry. The saved ASan stack places this exact call site immediately below the two `loop()` frames.

The first pattern byte is `'*'`, so `loop()` immediately recurses on `p + 1` before inspecting `s`. The recursive frame therefore parses only the bracket suffix `[][`, which is the portion that triggers the over-read.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned char *pp = p + 1; /* cannot handle with pointer to register */
if(setcharset(&pp, charset)) {
fine_trace.note: In the recursive frame from step 3, the first byte is `'['`, so `pp` aliases the bytes after the opening bracket. For the witness `pp` starts at the three-byte sequence `']'`, `'['`, `\0`, and `setcharset()` is asked to parse that bracket expression.

On entry `setcharset()` is in `CURLFNM_SCHS_DEFAULT`, and the first byte after `'['` is `']'`. Because `something_found` is still false, `']'` is accepted as a literal charset member, `state` becomes `CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBR`, and `*p` advances to the following `'['`.

With `state == CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBR` from step 5 and `*p` now on `'['`, this branch treats `'['` as another literal member, switches to `CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBRLEFTBR`, and advances `*p` to the terminating NUL.

Root cause. In `CURLFNM_SCHS_RIGHTBRLEFTBR`, the only closing case is `']'`. When step 6 has advanced `*p` to the terminator, `c == '\0'` falls into this generic else-arm because the function lacks the later fix's early `if(!c) return SETCHARSET_FAIL;`. The branch therefore records `charset[0]`, resets `state`, and increments `*p` one byte past the heap string.

Sink. The next `for(;;)` iteration rereads `**p` after step 7 moved `*p` past the NUL terminator, so this byte load touches 1 byte beyond the allocated `wildcard->pattern` buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line and points to step 1's `strdup()` as the allocation context.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged patch inserts `if(!c) return SETCHARSET_FAIL;` immediately after `c = **p;` in `setcharset()`, so the witnessed `c == '\0'` path at step 7 returns failure instead of incrementing `*p` past the duplicated pattern buffer. The patch also removes two now-redundant per-state `c == '\0'` checks.

format.name: curl_fuzzer TLV stream
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact TLV witness in `gt_results/arvo_42505099/poc`. Its verified trigger semantics are: a type-1 URL TLV whose effective C-string URL ends in `/test-list/*[][`, a type-33 `WILDCARDMATCH` TLV whose 4-byte value is `1`, and FTP response TLVs that drive the client through login/CWD/EPSV/TYPE/LIST so curl parses at least one directory entry and calls `ftp_pl_insert_finfo()` on that wildcard path. The staged evidence proves only this exact malformed bracket suffix `*[][` on the wildcard-enabled FTP `LIST` path, not broader fnmatch patterns or FTP transcripts.
